Figure 10.6 Transcription and Translation
When genes are expressed, the genetic information (base sequence) on DNA 
is ﬁ rst transcribed (copied) to a molecule of messenger RNA in a process 
similar to DNA replication. The mRNA molecules then leave the cell nucleus 
and enter the cytoplasm, where triplets of mRNA bases (codons) forming the 
genetic code specify the particular amino acids that make up an individual 
protein. This process, called translation, is accomplished by ribosomes 
(cellular components composed of proteins and another class of RNA) that 
read the genetic code from the mRNA, and by transfer RNAs (tRNAs) that 
transport the corresponding amino acids to the ribosomes for attachment to 
the growing protein.
